answer: Independent underwriters price the risk of a seat proving to be a clone and pay the network when it does. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. The sonnet is the premium, the yarrow the underwriting pool that pays on a clone proof, and the summit the correlated funding that sets the price; the sonnet scales with the summit, and the yarrow only pays when the clone is actually proved.
